Shetharboznai
SHEE-thar-BOZ-nye
proper noun
Aramaic Shethar Boznay (H8370), a Persian name of uncertain meaning; he is always named with Tatnai and their companions the Apharsachites.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Shetharboznai was a Persian officer associated with Tatnai, governor of the province Beyond the River, in the reign of Darius. He never appears alone. Three times the Authorized Version names him in the same breath as his governor — at the inquiry (Tatnai… and Shetharboznai, and their companions, Ezr 5:3), in the letter to Darius (Ezr 5:6), and in the obedient execution of the king's reply (Ezr 6:13). He is a second officer, a co-signatory, one of the companions; and the chief thing Scripture records of him is that when the decree came back from Susa confirming the Jews' right to build, he did what he was told, speedily. The episode is a small study in the sort of opposition that turns out not to be opposition. Ezra 4 had shown the malicious kind, where Rehum and Shimshai wrote a letter designed to stop the work and then made them to cease by force and power. Ezra 5 shows the procedural kind, which asks its question, records the answer, refers upward, and abides by the result. The Jews built straight through the second sort, because the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews (Ezr 5:5).

Origin & Era

A Persian officer of the province Beyond the River under Darius, named always with Tatnai the governor in the inquiry into the rebuilding of the temple.

expand to see more

SHETHARBOZNAI, Aramaic Shethar Boznay, a Persian name of uncertain signification.

An officer of the province Beyond the River in the reign of Darius.

Named with Tatnai the governor and their companions the Apharsachites.

He joined in questioning the Jews concerning the rebuilding of the house of God.

When Darius confirmed the decree of Cyrus, he executed it speedily with Tatnai.

Key Scripture

Ezr 5:3 — "At the same time came to them Tatnai, governor on this side the river, and Shetharboznai, and their companions, and said thus unto them, Who hath commanded you to build this house, and to make up this wall?"

Ezr 5:6 — "The copy of the letter that Tatnai, governor on this side the river, and Shetharboznai, and his companions the Apharsachites, which were on this side the river, sent unto Darius the king:"

Ezr 6:13 — "Then Tatnai, governor on this side the river, Shetharboznai, and their companions, according to that which Darius the king had sent, so they did speedily."

Ezr 4:24 — "Then ceased the work of the house of God which is at Jerusalem. So it ceased unto the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia."

Modern Corruption

Every question put to the church is heard as an attack; Scripture distinguishes lawful inquiry from malicious opposition.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Shetharboznai has no modern partisans. The discernment his story requires is nevertheless in short supply. Believers under pressure easily lose the ability to tell the difference between a hostile act and a fair question, and treat both as persecution. Ezra sets the two side by side on purpose. In chapter 4 the work is stopped by a letter written in bad faith, followed by force and power. In chapter 5 the work continues while officials ask who authorised it and write to the king to find out.

Scripture expects the church to be able to answer an inquiry. Be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear (1Pe 3:15), and the elders of the Jews did precisely that — they gave their names, their history, and the decree they were relying on. The principle to recover is that a clear conscience welcomes examination. A work that cannot survive an honest question was never going to survive a real attack, and treating every questioner as an enemy makes enemies of people God has sent to test whether we are telling the truth.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Aramaic Shethar Boznay (H8370), a Persian personal name; associated with the Apharsachites, a class of Persian officials.

expand to see more

Aramaic Shethar Boznay (H8370) — the officer named with Tatnai; Ezra 5:3, 5:6, 6:6, 6:13.

Aramaic Apharsakay (H671) — the Apharsachites, a class or people among the Persian officialdom.

Aramaic kenath (H3675) — a companion, a colleague; the word rendered their companions.

Aramaic taam (H2942) — a decree, a command; the royal word that settled the question.

Hebrew batel (H989) — to cease, to make to cease; the verb of Ezra 4:24.

Usage

"“Tatnai… and Shetharboznai, and their companions” — the phrase that always carries him."

"“His companions the Apharsachites, which were on this side the river”."

"“According to that which Darius the king had sent, so they did speedily”."
